newsitem.title: USA: Ribozyme sees testing first half of '97.
newsitem.headline: Ribozyme sees testing first half of '97.

text.p: Ribozyme Pharmaceuticals Inc chief executive officer Ralph Christofferson said on Thursday the company is on target to start clinical trials the first half of this year on a gene therapy approach using ribozymes against HIV.
He told the Colorado Bio Investment Conference the approach uses multiple ribozymes, which is key to preventing the virus from developing resisitance to therapy.

"Each of the ribozymes in the construct is designed to attack a different point in the HIV gene," he told the conference. "So if the HIV gene finds a way to mutate against one of these sites, all of the other sites can still be effective," he said.
Ribozymes are ribonucleic acid molecules that can catalyze a number of chemical reactions.
The clinical trials will be carried out as part of a collaboration with Chiron Corp, the City of Hope and Childrens Hospital Los Angeles, he said.
